lines.trans: Nastya, do you know where to rent a flat?
I was looking for a place myself this morning.
And did you manage to find a room?
Kostik helped me, I am moving to his place.
Wait, Kostya invited you to live together?
Yes, after all he and I are dating.
To be honest, I do not envy you at all.
Why? Kostya is such a sweet guy.
At night he snores terribly and loudly!
Oh, I cannot stand snoring at all!
Think well before agreeing.
You are right, I will look for another option.

meanings.note: других вариантов нет = there are no other options

examples.text: Пробуем, других вариантов у нас нет.
examples.trans: Let's try it, we have no other options.

examples.text: Это самый лучший вариант для всех.
examples.trans: This is the very best option for everyone.

examples.text: Трава, говорите? Отлично! Пробуем, других вариантов у нас нет.
examples.trans: Herbs, you say? Excellent! Let's try it, we have no other options.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('after all') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I did tell you, you know!

examples.text: Садись, не бойся. Я ведь сам чуть тебя не отпустил.
examples.trans: Sit down, don't be afraid. I very nearly let you go myself.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'together'.

examples.text: Мы с Пашей вместе уже месяц.
examples.trans: Pasha and I have been together for a month now.

встречаться.gloss: to meet; to date, to go out

meanings.en: to date, to go out (with someone)
meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'тречаться'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to meet', forming an aspectual pair with 'встретиться'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.
Secondary conversational sense ('to meet up') (+ с + instrumental) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: We've been dating for a month.
We've been going out for a month already.

выносить.gloss: to bear, to tolerate; to carry out

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'носить'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to bear', forming an aspectual pair with 'вынести'.

examples.text: Ой, я совсем не выношу храп!
examples.trans: Oh, I cannot stand snoring at all!
Come on, let us bring the caviar into the hall.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'where'.

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to speak', forming an aspectual pair with 'сказать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to speak, to talk') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
поставить громко = to put a phone on speaker

examples.text: Не говорите так громко, дети спят.
examples.trans: Don't speak so loudly, the children are asleep.

examples.text: Ой, это Илона! Я громко поставлю.
examples.trans: Oh, it's Ilona! I'll put it on speaker.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Secondary conversational sense ('? = really?, oh yeah?') (disbelief) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('other, another, different').
Secondary conversational sense ('different') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Послушайте, а можно в другое место? Здесь плохо пахнет.
examples.trans: Listen, could we go somewhere else? It smells bad in here.

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'housing', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: We are looking for inexpensive housing.
They are looking for inexpensive housing.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to live'.

examples.trans: I live in a communal flat.

examples.text: Я хочу нормально жить! Я хочу биде, понимаешь?
examples.trans: I want to live like a normal person! I want a bidet, do you understand?

завидовать.gloss: to envy, to be jealous of

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'видовать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to envy', forming an aspectual pair with 'позавидовать'.

examples.trans: I envy you in a good way.

examples.text: У него было ружьё. Все мальчишки завидовали ему.
examples.trans: He had an air gun. All the boys envied him.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to know'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'кать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to look for'.

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'to' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'flat', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: Do you remember the toilet in the communal flat?

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'room', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
милый / милая used as a form of address
милый / милая used as a form of address
нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to find', paired with 'находить'.

examples.text: Ну где я сейчас найду грузчиков?
examples.trans: Well, where am I going to find movers right now?

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
ночью = at night; спокойной ночи = good night

examples.text: Ну что, Аркаша? Наступила ночь, просыпается мафия.
examples.trans: So, Arkasha? Night has fallen, the mafia wakes up.

meanings.note: Expressive conversational Russian interjection or greeting ('oh') used directly in spoken exchanges.
accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
Secondary conversational sense ('it') (for masculine and neuter things) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Declinable masculine noun meaning 'boyfriend', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('guy, lad, young man') (informal) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

переезжать.gloss: to move (house), to relocate; to cross

meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'езжать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to move', forming an aspectual pair with 'переехать'.

examples.text: Ну и что? Я всё равно переезжать собираюсь.
examples.trans: So what? I'm planning to move anyway.

examples.text: Переезжай ко мне в большую квартиру.
examples.trans: Move in with me into a big apartment.

meanings.note: mostly the imperative: погоди! = wait!; ну, погоди! = just you wait!

meanings.en: to think it over, to give it a thought
meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'умать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to think', forming an aspectual pair with 'думать'.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'звать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to call, summon', paired with 'звать'.

examples.text: Дядя Аркадий всё починит и позовёт.
examples.trans: Uncle Arkady will fix everything and call you.

examples.text: Главное, чтобы она не позвала директора.
examples.trans: The main thing is that she does not call the director.

поискать.gloss: to look for, to search a bit

meanings.en: to search for a while, to look around
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'искать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to look for', forming an aspectual pair with 'искать'.

examples.trans: I will look for another option.
You are right, I will look for another option.

examples.text: Может, стоит поискать причины в себе?
examples.trans: Maybe you should look at yourself for the reasons?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мочь'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to help', forming an aspectual pair with 'помогать'.

examples.text: Экскаваторщик — это не мой уровень. Может, поможешь?
examples.trans: Excavator driver isn't my level. Maybe you could help?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'why'.

examples.trans: Why are we going so slowly?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'right', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('right, correct') (short form: ты прав = you're right) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Заходите. Поставьте, пожалуйста, правую ногу на кровать.
examples.trans: Come in. Please put your right foot on the bed.

meanings.note: adverb or conjunction in 'прежде чем'
+ instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('oneself') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

сдать.gloss: to return, to hand in; to pass (an exam)

meanings.en: to return, to hand back, to turn in
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'дать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to return', forming an aspectual pair with 'сдавать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to pass') (an exam: сдать экзамен) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Нам надо сдать машину до десяти часов.
examples.trans: We have to return the car before ten o'clock.

examples.text: Я за комнаткой пригляжу. Может, сдам кому, а денежки пополам!
examples.trans: I'll look after the little room. Maybe I'll rent it to someone, and we'll split the money!

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'today'.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'quite'.
Secondary conversational sense ('not at all') (совсем не) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: That's not what I mean at all.

examples.text: Нет, Вика, я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: No, Vika, that's not what I mean at all.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'оглашаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to agree', paired with 'согласиться'.

examples.text: Вот стою и думаю, соглашаться или нет.
examples.trans: Here I stand and think, whether to agree or not.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'scary'.

examples.trans: Did you really suddenly get scared?

examples.text: Он ночью страшно и громко храпит!
examples.trans: At night he snores terribly and loudly!

meanings.note: 'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I
Secondary conversational sense ('? = what's this?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.en: to turn out well, to succeed, to manage (impersonal + dative)
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'даться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to succeed, to manage', paired with 'удаваться'.

examples.text: Я не поняла, как тебе это удалось.
examples.trans: I didn't understand how you managed that.
And did you manage to find a room?

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'morning', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'well'.
Secondary conversational sense ('good, fine') (as an answer) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Хорошо, Виктор Петрович, я сейчас же всё переделаю заново!
examples.trans: All right, Viktor Petrovich, I will redo everything right now!

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'snoring', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Ой, я совсем не выношу храп!
examples.trans: Oh, I cannot stand snoring at all!

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to snore', forming an aspectual pair with 'захрапеть'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Он ночью страшно и громко храпит!
examples.trans: At night he snores terribly and loudly!

meanings.note: in comparisons: больше, чем = more than

examples.text: А почему нет? Продавец получает больше, чем преподаватель.
examples.trans: Why not? A sales assistant earns more than a lecturer.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Do you want me to tell you honestly?

examples.text: Всё честно, Лёха. Взрослые не умеют ждать.
examples.trans: It's all fair, Lyokha. Grown-ups can't wait.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
